correctness.rationale: For any circular four-run binary word, cutting creates four or five linear source runs; reverse-complement palindromes have an even number of runs, hence exactly two or four. A two-run optimum draws either the two runs of one color and one of the other or vice versa, yielding P. A four-run optimum draws four consecutive source runs and its paired mirrored lengths give Q. For balanced totals s, the identities P=s/2+U and Q=s-U+V imply A/2>=3s/4, while explicit positive quadruples attain the ceiling for every s. When four divides s, equality forces U=s/4,V=0. Independent interval DP on every rotation checked 4096 tuples; explicit mask enumeration checked 495 smaller tuples; balanced exhaustive maxima and constructions checked to s=50. Finite checks are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The four-run case is the first nontrivial fixed-run endpoint of a proposed separated-matching hierarchy. An exact closed formula valid also for unbalanced circles, every finite balanced optimum, and rigorous equality characterization identify a meaningful structural boundary, rather than a new numerical instance or trivial renaming. The unrestricted fixed-run conjecture is false in general, making the rigorously surviving k=2 boundary of specific interest.
